environment.neo4j: 5.26.31 community (Compose image from compose.yaml), heap max 512 MiB, page cache 256 MiB
environment.note: Run on the development machine with the real Compose services, after the M3 branch was merged with main.

container_memory_gib.note: docker stats takes about 2 s per sample, so the peak is indicative

dump_load_with_documented_commands.dump: docker compose stop neo4j; docker compose run --rm -v <dir>:/dumps neo4j neo4j-admin database dump neo4j --to-path=/dumps; docker compose up -d --wait neo4j
dump_load_with_documented_commands.load: docker compose -p qihuang-restore run --rm -v <dir>:/dumps neo4j neo4j-admin database load neo4j --from-path=/dumps --overwrite-destination=true (an isolated Compose project, so the development volume was not overwritten), then a temporary instance on 127.0.0.1:27687
dump_load_with_documented_commands.pitfall: The dump directory must be writable by the container's neo4j user (UID 7474). An existing var/neo4j-dumps owned by that user cannot be written or listed by the host user: the dump then fails, and a later load silently restores whatever older dump is in the directory. Check the dump file's size and file count before loading.
